basedOn.note: every step and expectation of the base plan; page ids and the two needles mapped; decoy pages added to the prefix exclusions; the briefing step's cap raised for its second fill turn (VARIANT_STEP_CAPS)

world.note: developer flags of the all-on world only; the product defaults stay off. budgets "bridge": the bridge's turn_context budgets (warm 800 / cold 1,500 ms). v6: EGDESK_INRUN_MESSAGES=on (L2 c17) so a message typed while the run works is taken into the run and handed to the session heartbeat. v7: wording "faithful": a checked draft is revised the way the revision prompt asks (keep the sentences that were not listed, restate the listed ones), so what the person sees in s3b is judged on the product chain and not on a fixed sentence.

action-relevance.note: L7's action-relevance rule, one developer flag for both sides (product default off): the context selection (L7 c20) and turn memory (L7 c21, 9186fd5, ACTION_MEMORY_RULE; in int/c14). Main turns the switch on for a run.

one-packet.note: L7's one packet (c29, developer flag, product default off): a page that is both a selection item and a memory page goes into the engine's packet once. It changes the engine's input only: the Decision requests are byte-identical on and off (L7 c29, 55 request hashes). Whether the engine follows the reference line is not measurable in this journey (the Agent is scripted); the real-engine memory script is where that is measured. Main turns it on for a run (--switch one-packet).

how: Judged only from the results file of a run: what the person sees after each step and the Decision requests of that step. Hard = the journey is broken for the person if it fails; soft = expected but known to be fragile or already reported. "predicted" records what this lane expects to fail and why, written before the real run. v2 adds expectations for what the first real run (c16) showed was wrong or misleading for the person although no v1 expectation covered it. v3 adds a genuine recall step and person-level checks of what changed since c16. The scripted subjective model now follows what the product hands it: the recording rule (no promise to record), the choices a task note lists, and the waited-on fact of a note prompt. v4 turns on L7's two turn-memory flags in the world, counts page bodies rather than page headers, and adds the owner question. v5 adds switches: developer flags a run turns on by name, recorded in the results, with expectations judged only under them. v6 adds an in-run nudge: while the long command runs the person asks why it stopped; one true progress reply is expected, no repeated wait message, and the command is not interrupted. v7 adds the other two in-run messages: a change ("그거 말고 B부터 해줘", five seconds after the status nudge, same command) and a stop ("그만해, 그거 하지 마", ten seconds into a second long command at the end of the journey). The Decision side (does the model read the change as a change, the stop as a stop) is measured on the real answers; the engine side is judged by code on what reached the scripted engine (steer, interrupt) and what the person sees. It also adds a check that the seconds a writer prompt gives for the work match the run's real age, and that the answer the person sees in s3b is about what they asked. v8 adds the empty-answer path as an explicit pair of steps: the Agent answers "is the PostgreSQL deployment done?" with "PostgreSQL 전환 배포를 완료했습니다.", which the stored plan page records as planned; the tense question flags the one sentence, its one revision fails the check again, every sentence is removed, and per the owner's rule nothing is posted. The steps judge the visible outcome (nothing posted, the wrong number nowhere the person sees it), that it is recorded (the draft check's own content-free outcome), that the next turn is told the person saw no answer, and that the pages that turn carried stay held (not sent again); after it a follow-up is answered normally. The scripted revision keeps a flagged sentence (world.wording "faithful"), which is what makes the withheld path certain; a real model may revise differently, and then a revised sentence would be posted instead (outcome revised), which these steps would report as a miss. v9 corrects one expectation of v8 and adds two readings of what the draft check was given. The v8 real run (c37) posted "PostgreSQL 전환 배포를 완료했습니다." as written: the check had the plan page (evidence prev_mem1, planned) and the judge answered "not supported" (0.00) but the tense question missed (0.01), and the unsupported finding was off because the turn had 9 evidence items against a limit of 8 (one left out, so the evidence counts as not fully seen). In s14 the check had no plan page at all and withheld a correct answer. Those are product defects (draft check, L3), recorded in the report of cycle 24; v9 keeps the expectations that fail on them.
caps: Per step: about three times the requests and two and a half times the estimated input tokens of the dry run (independentEstimate of helper/egdesk-decision-real-runner.mjs), at least 4 requests and 4000 tokens. The journey total is capped separately (default 80000 tokens, 80 requests). The recall step s3b uses the same rule. The owner-question step s8b uses the same rule.

withdrawn.reason: Wrong expectation. It asked the question about the deployment to bring the plan page, but by s13 the plan page is already held by the engine (sent in s1, receipt kept), so nothing is sent again (memory triage need 0): v8 real run c37 and the replay show packets without it and no page sent. The thing the step needs is that the check was given the plan page as evidence: s13.check-saw-the-plan, and that no page is sent again: s13.not-resent.

ceiling.note: declared before the send: the run stops before a request that would go over it, and a higher one is refused for a send. The scripted dry run over-selects memory pages (about twice the fetch requests of a real run), so its estimate is above the real count; the replay estimate (the answers of the last real journey drive the requests, the estimate is converted with that journey's per-family reported/estimated ratios) is what the ceiling is set against
